topic.title: Dermatology residency education in the treatment of testosterone-induced acne and androgenic alopecia in trans men: a cross-sectional survey of academic dermatologists in the USA
topic.abstract: This cross-sectional survey study explores the experience, comfort and knowledge of dermatology residents and attendings in managing testosterone-induced acne (TiAV) and androgenic alopecia (TiAGA) in trans men. While most respondents reported some level of comfort treating these conditions, objective knowledge scores were modest and revealed gaps across both conditions, particularly TiAGA. Our findings suggest that current LGBTQIA+-focused education may be perceived as adequate but may not translate into knowledge retention or clinical preparedness.

sentences: The majority agreed that their programmes emphasized inclusive language (n = 42/50; 84%), gender identity-­inclusive history taking (n = 39/50; 78%) and exposure to multidisciplinary care models (n = 39/50; 78%).

Lower agreement was reported for training related to gender identity and expression (n = 30/50; 60%), overall preparedness for caring for gender-­diverse patients (n = 30/50; 60%), and LGBTQIA + research and advocacy (n = 29/50; 58%).

[논문 정보]
제목: Dermatology residency education in the treatment of testosterone-induced acne and androgenic alopecia in trans men: a cross-sectional survey of academic dermatologists in the USA
저널: Skin health and disease
저자: Nguyen TQ, Neubauer Z, Zaladonis A 외
발행: 2026 Dec
원문: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/43094833/

[한눈에 보기]
- This cross-sectional survey study explores the experience, comfort and knowledge of dermatology residents and attendings in managing testosterone-induced acne (TiAV) and androgenic alopecia (TiAGA) in trans men.
- While most respondents reported some level of comfort treating these conditions, objective knowledge scores were modest and revealed gaps across both conditions, particularly TiAGA.
- Our findings suggest that current LGBTQIA+-focused education may be perceived as adequate but may not translate into knowledge retention or clinical preparedness.

◆ 그 밖의 내용 — 본문
  · The majority agreed that their programmes emphasized inclusive language (n = 42/50; 84%), gender identity-­inclusive history taking (n = 39/50; 78%) and exposure to multidisciplinary care models (n = 39/50; 78%).
  · Lower agreement was reported for training related to gender identity and expression (n = 30/50; 60%), overall preparedness for caring for gender-­diverse patients (n = 30/50; 60%), and LGBTQIA + research and advocacy (n = 29/50; 58%).
